assumptions.condition: For each \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and have common law \(\mathbb P\).

For every \(\mathbb P\) under consideration and every \(x\in[d]\) with \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)>0\), the conditional probability \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) satisfies \(\epsilon\leq\pi_x\leq1-\epsilon\).

definitions.name: causal completion class for the observed discrete experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}:=\{P:P\text{ is a law of }(X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\text{ with }X\in[d],\ A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\},\ P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency}\text{ and }\mathrm{ass:conditional-exchangeability},\text{ and }\operatorname{Obs}(P)\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\}\) for every \(d\geq2\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).

definitions.name: four-cell overlap cone
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_\epsilon:=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\leq s_1(u)\leq(1-\epsilon)s(u)\}\), where \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\) and \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\).

definitions.name: globally Lipschitz observational cell-value extension
definitions.construction: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define \(g_{a,\epsilon}(u):=s(u)u_{a1}/\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon(u):=\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}g_{a,\epsilon}(u)\); set \(g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0\).

definitions.name: causal unrestricted oracle value
definitions.construction: \(V^\star(P):=E_P[\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}]\).  This is a full-data causal functional; its equality to an observed-law functional is asserted only by \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\).

definitions.name: bounded-alphabet empirical-ratio fallback
definitions.construction: Let \(\overline N_x=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\), \(\overline N_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}\), and \(\overline S_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}\). Put \(\widehat p_x=\overline N_x/n\), \(\widehat\mu_{ax}=\overline S_{ax}/\overline N_{ax}\) with \(0/0=0\), and \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}=\sum_{x=1}^d\widehat p_x\max_a\widehat\mu_{ax}\).

definitions.name: positive order-four tensor Jackson approximation
definitions.construction: For integer \(K_d\geq2\), let \(J_{K_d}(t)=c_{K_d}[\sin(K_dt/2)/\sin(t/2)]^4\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), with removable values filled continuously and \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that \(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1\). For a rectangle \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) with center \(b_{\jmath,x}=(\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x})/2\) and radius \(r_{\jmath,x}=(u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x})/2\), define \(P_{x,K_d}\) by the even product convolution \(P_{x,K_d}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}\bar f_\epsilon(b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t))\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_{K_d}(t_{\jmath})\,dt\).

definitions.name: explicit all-data pilot-local Jackson--factorial estimator
definitions.construction: Put \(L_d=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), and \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L_d\rfloor\}\). If \(d<D_0\), return \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\); if \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), return \(1/2\). Otherwise draw \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\), and on \(M\leq n\) mark the first \(M\) observations independently by \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), producing independent pilot and evaluation counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) and \(N_{\jmath,x}\); on \(M>n\), set the randomized output to zero. For \(M\leq n\), let \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\), \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}=\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\}\), \(u_{\jmath,x}=c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x}\), and \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\), with center \(b_x\) and coordinate radii \(r_x\). Expand \(P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}((v-b_x)/r_x)^\alpha\). Define \(U_h(N;z)=\sum_{t=0}^h\binom ht(-z)^{h-t}(N)_t/m^t\), \(S_x=(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}r_{\jmath,x}\), \(Z_x=\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath}U_{\alpha_{\jmath}}(N_{\jmath,x};b_{\jmath,x})/r_{\jmath,x}^{\alpha_{\jmath}}\), and \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}=\Pi_{[\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)-d^{1/4}S_x,\,\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+d^{1/4}S_x]}(Z_x)\). The randomized statistic is \(\widetilde V=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\sum_xT_x^{\mathrm{JF}})\). In the Jackson branch define the all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}:=E[\widetilde V\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n]\), where the conditional expectation integrates only the displayed auxiliary Poisson count and marks.

definitions.name: equal-propensity normalized \(L_1\) subexperiment
definitions.construction: For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), set \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), and complete the observed law with conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes, treatment propensity \(1/2\), and consistency.

definitions.name: observed-margin map
definitions.construction: For a full-data law \(P\), define its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) by \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\{(x,a,y)\}=P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\) for \((x,a,y)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^2\).

definitions.name: published unrestricted observed discrete-confounder law class
definitions.construction:
\(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the set of all laws \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which there are \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\Delta_d\), \(\pi_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and \(\mu_{ax}\in[0,1]\) satisfying, for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 q_{a1,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},\qquad
 q_{a0,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax}),
\]
where \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\).  Thus the support contains at most \(d\) covariate cells; the parameters on a null cell may be chosen arbitrarily within their displayed ranges.

definitions.name: observed-law optimal-regression value
definitions.construction: For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) with table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\), define the observed-law optimal-regression functional by \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\Psi(\mathbf q):=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}\).  This value is independent of the permitted choice of \(\mu_{ax}\) on cells with \(p_x=0\).

definitions.name: observed-law optimal-value minimax mean-squared error
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable maps from \(([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\).

definitions.name: overlap-cone approximation--moment dual handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) is the route that rescales the pilot-local four-cell rectangles by their Poisson noise geometry, optimizes the tensor-polynomial bias--variance functional for \(\bar f_\epsilon\), and dualizes the approximation constraint into moment-matched observed laws in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for the target \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\).

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), one has \(q_x\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\) and \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^d\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\).  Moreover, \(0\leq\bar f_\epsilon(u)\leq s(u)\) and \(\lvert\bar f_\epsilon(u)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\rvert\leq(1+\epsilon^{-1})\lVert u-v\rVert_1\) for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\).  Every \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) has a completion \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) with \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)=\mathbb P\), obtained by drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes with means \(\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\), then drawing \(A\) independently of their joint vector given \(X\), and setting \(Y=Y(A)\); conversely, \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\).
statements.justification: The extension and completion equivalence put off-cone pilots, null cells, and the causal interpretation on a single rigorously separated foundation.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete separates the observed functional from causal identification but does not provide this global four-cell Lipschitz extension or the optimal-value completion statement.
statements.consumer: The Jackson proof works on every observed pilot rectangle, while causal users get an explicit completion check.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:observed-model-class}\), choose parameters \(p_x,\pi_x,\mu_{ax}\) in the displayed ranges.  Summing the two outcome probabilities in arm \(a\) gives
\[
 s_a(q_x)=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a},\qquad s(q_x)=p_x,
 \qquad q_{a1,x}=s_a(q_x)\mu_{ax}.                                  \tag{1}
\]
If \(p_x>0\), the bound \(\epsilon\leq\pi_x\leq1-\epsilon\) in \(\mathrm{def:observed-model-class}\) implies
\(\epsilon s(q_x)\leq s_1(q_x)\leq(1-\epsilon)s(q_x)\); if \(p_x=0\), then \(q_x=0\) and the same inequalities hold.  Hence \(q_x\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\) by \(\mathrm{def:overlap-cone}\).  On this cone, \(s_a(q_x)\geq\epsilon s(q_x)\), so (1) and \(\mathrm{def:global-extension}\) yield
\[
 g_{a,\epsilon}(q_x)=\frac{s(q_x)q_{a1,x}}{s_a(q_x)}=p_x\mu_{ax},
 \qquad \bar f_\epsilon(q_x)=p_x\max_a\mu_{ax}                    \tag{2}
\]
on occupied cells.  Both sides of (2) are zero on null cells.  Summing (2) and invoking \(\mathrm{def:observed-optimal-value}\) proves \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_x\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\).

For the global bounds, put \(D_a(u)=\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\).  Because \(0\leq u_{a1}\leq s_a(u)\leq D_a(u)\),
\[
 0\leq g_{a,\epsilon}(u)=\frac{s(u)u_{a1}}{D_a(u)}\leq s(u),        \tag{3}
\]
and (3) passes to the maximum over \(a\).  On \(s_a(u)\leq\epsilon s(u)\), one has \(g_{a,\epsilon}(u)=u_{a1}/\epsilon\), whose coordinate derivatives have absolute value at most \(\epsilon^{-1}\).  On \(s_a(u)\geq\epsilon s(u)\), write \(S=s(u)\), \(t=s_a(u)\), and \(z=u_{a1}\).  The derivatives of \(Sz/t\), respectively in a coordinate outside arm \(a\), the success coordinate in arm \(a\), and the failure coordinate in arm \(a\), are
\[
 \frac zt,\qquad \frac zt+\frac St\left(1-\frac zt\right),
 \qquad \frac zt-\frac St\frac zt.                                \tag{4}
\]
Here \(0\leq z/t\leq1\) and \(S/t\leq\epsilon^{-1}\), so every derivative in (4) has absolute value at most \(1+\epsilon^{-1}\).  The two formulas agree on \(t=\epsilon S\).  A line segment in \(\mathbb R_+^4\setminus\{0\}\) is divided by this hyperplane into at most two nontrivial pieces, and integration of the coordinate-gradient bound along those pieces gives
\[
 |g_{a,\epsilon}(u)-g_{a,\epsilon}(v)|
 \leq(1+\epsilon^{-1})\lVert u-v\rVert_1.                           \tag{5}
\]
At the origin, (5) follows by continuity and (3), since \(s(u)=\lVert u\rVert_1\).  Finally,
\[
 |\max_a g_{a,\epsilon}(u)-\max_a g_{a,\epsilon}(v)|
 \leq\max_a|g_{a,\epsilon}(u)-g_{a,\epsilon}(v)|,
\]
which proves the asserted Lipschitz bound, including coordinate faces and tie surfaces.

It remains to prove equivalence of the experiments.  For the chosen parameters of \(\mathbb P\), draw \(X\) with masses \(p_x\); conditional on \(X=x\), draw \(Y(0)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_{0x})\) and \(Y(1)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_{1x})\) independently, draw \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_x)\) independently of their joint vector, and set \(Y=Y(A)\).  This construction satisfies consistency, satisfies the armwise conditional independence in \(\mathrm{ass:conditional-exchangeability}\), and has its observed margin equal to \(\mathbb P\) by the two formulas in \(\mathrm{def:observed-model-class}\).  Its observed margin also has the required overlap, so \(\mathrm{def:model-class}\) places the completion in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\).  Conversely, if \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), then \(\mathrm{def:model-class}\) states that its observed margin belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  This proves both directions, including arbitrary null cells and boundary means.

statements.statement: Let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) have center \(b_x\) and positive radii \(r_{\jmath,x}\). The single polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-kernel}\) has coordinate degree \(2(K_d-1)\) and satisfies, for every \(v\in Q_x\), \(\lvert P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\rvert\leq C_\epsilon\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\{\sqrt{(v_{\jmath}-\ell_{\jmath,x})(u_{\jmath,x}-v_{\jmath})}/K_d+r_{\jmath,x}/K_d^2\}\). If \(P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}((v-b_x)/r_x)^\alpha\), then \(\sum_\alpha\lvert b_{x,\alpha}\rvert\leq A^{K_d}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}r_{\jmath,x}\) for a universal \(A<\infty\). Both bounds hold for the same polynomial when \(Q_x\) touches the origin, a coordinate face, or a treatment-effect tie surface.
statements.justification: This is the exact certificate the parent could not supply: pointwise vertex adaptation and the centered coefficient envelope are properties of one explicit polynomial.
statements.gap: JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 localizes a two-dimensional absolute difference and CaiLow2011L1 controls scalar absolute-value approximation; neither proves the joint four-dimensional observational-ratio certificate.
statements.consumer: The centered factorial lift uses the coefficient envelope while the global bias calculation uses the pointwise bound, so this lemma connects both halves of the estimator proof.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(B=1+\epsilon^{-1}\), which is a Lipschitz constant for \(\bar f_\epsilon\) by \(\mathrm{prop:identification-and-extension}\).  Suppress the cell subscript and write \(Q=\prod_{j=1}^4[\ell_j,u_j]\), \(b_j=(\ell_j+u_j)/2\), and \(r_j=(u_j-\ell_j)/2>0\).  For \(K=K_d\), define
\[
 H(\vartheta)=\bar f_\epsilon(b+r\odot\cos\vartheta),
 \qquad
 \mathcal J_KH(\vartheta)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}H(\vartheta+t)\prod_{j=1}^4J_K(t_j)\,dt.
\]
This is exactly the construction in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-kernel}\).

The elementary inequalities
\[
 \left|\frac{\sin(Kt/2)}{\sin(t/2)}\right|
 \leq C\min\{K,|t|^{-1}\},
 \qquad |t|\leq\pi,
\]
and the reverse bound on \(|t|\leq K^{-1}\) show that the unnormalized fourth power has integral between constant multiples of \(K^3\).  Hence its normalized version obeys
\[
 0\leq J_K(t)\leq\frac{CK}{(1+K|t|)^4},\qquad
 \int|t|J_K(t)\,dt\leq\frac CK,\qquad
 \int t^2J_K(t)\,dt\leq\frac C{K^2}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
The fourth power is an even trigonometric polynomial of degree \(2(K-1)\).  Convolution therefore makes \(\mathcal J_KH\) an even trigonometric polynomial, separately in each coordinate, of coordinate degree at most \(2(K-1)\).  Since an even trigonometric polynomial of degree \(D\) is a polynomial of degree \(D\) in \(\cos\vartheta\), this defines the polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) in the statement with the asserted coordinate degree.

If \(v=b+r\odot\cos\vartheta\), Taylor's formula for cosine with second derivative bounded by one gives
\[
 r_j|\cos(\vartheta_j+t_j)-\cos\vartheta_j|
 \leq r_j|\sin\vartheta_j|\,|t_j|+\frac12r_jt_j^2.
\]
Moreover
\[
 r_j|\sin\vartheta_j|=\sqrt{(v_j-\ell_j)(u_j-v_j)}.
\]
Apply the \(B\)-Lipschitz inequality to the integrand, integrate with (1), and sum over the four coordinates.  This proves
\[
 |P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)|
 \leq C_\epsilon\sum_{j=1}^4\left\{
 \frac{\sqrt{(v_j-\ell_j)(u_j-v_j)}}{K_d}+\frac{r_j}{K_d^2}
 \right\}.                                                               \tag{2}
\]

For the coefficient assertion, positivity and normalization of the product kernel imply
\[
 \sup_{v\in Q}|P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b)|
 \leq B\sum_{j=1}^4r_j=:S.                                               \tag{3}
\]
Expand the left side of (3) in the tensor Chebyshev basis on \([-1,1]^4\).  The cosine integral formula bounds each tensor Chebyshev coefficient by \(16S\).  If \(c_h\) denotes the sum of the absolute monomial coefficients of the Chebyshev polynomial \(T_h\), then \(T_{h+1}=2zT_h-T_{h-1}\) gives
\[
 c_{h+1}\leq2c_h+c_{h-1},\qquad c_0=c_1=1,\qquad
 c_h\leq(1+\sqrt2)^h.
\]
Writing \(D=2(K_d-1)\), multiplying the four one-dimensional bounds and summing over at most \((D+1)^4\) tensor coefficients gives
\[
 \sum_\alpha|b_{x,\alpha}|
 \leq16S(D+1)^4(1+\sqrt2)^{4D}
 \leq A^{K_d}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}
\]
for a universal finite \(A\).  Equations (2) and (3) concern the same convolution polynomial.  No part of the argument requires an interior rectangle or differentiability of \(\bar f_\epsilon\), so it applies when \(Q_x\) touches the origin, a coordinate face, or a tie surface.

statements.statement: In the uncapped Poisson comparison experiment induced by \(M\) and \(B_i\), conditional on the pilot counts the statistics \(U_h(N;z)\) satisfy \(E[U_h(N;z)]=(q-z)^h\) and \(E[U_h(N;z)U_t(N;z)]=\sum_{\ell=0}^{h\wedge t}\binom h\ell\binom t\ell\ell!(q/m)^\ell(q-z)^{h+t-2\ell}\). With the pilot rectangles and clipping in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), \(\lvert E[T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}]-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\rvert\leq C_\epsilon\{\sqrt{p_x/(mL_d)}+1/(mL_d)\}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}})\leq C_\epsilon d^{1/16}\{p_xL_d/m+L_d^2/m^2\}\). The contribution of pilot failure obeys these same local \(p_x\)-dependent scales.
statements.justification: The exact centered factorial identity prevents the polynomial center from reappearing in the variance, while local pilot tails prevent a dimension-only exceptional-event loss.
statements.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015Functionals and JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 use factorial moments after localization, but not with random four-coordinate ratio boxes, local clipping, and arbitrary cell masses.
statements.consumer: Summing these cell bounds yields the logarithmic upper rate without treating uncentered cell mean-squared errors as independent contributions.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the explicit all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) satisfies \(\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\).  The bound permits unknown unequal propensities, arbitrary occupied-cell masses, null cells, outcome means at zero or one, and exact treatment-effect ties.
statements.justification: This named estimator is uniformly rate-optimal on the full published observed-law class, not only on one potential-outcome representation.
statements.gap: The parent certifies only \(d/n\) risk; JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 does not cover unknown observational arm denominators.
statements.consumer: Categorical-adjustment analyses obtain a finite-sample worst-case benchmark allowing unequal propensities, null cells, and exact ties.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}extension}\) gives
\[
 0\leq\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_x\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)
 \leq\sum_xs(q_x)=1
\]
and supplies a completion \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) whose observed margin is \(\mathbb P\).  Every statistic below depends only on the observed sample and the displayed auxiliary variables, so its law under the completion is its law under \(\mathbb P\).  Hence \(\mathrm{lem:centered\mbox{-}factorial\mbox{-}pilot\mbox{-}control}\) applies uniformly over the full observed model.

First suppose \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n\geq d/L_d\), and put \(m=n/8\).  In the uncapped Poisson comparison experiment, counts belonging to distinct \(x\)'s are independent by Poisson splitting; therefore the clipped statistics \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\), including their pilot components, are independent.  The cell bias bound, \(\sum_xp_x=1\), and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \left|\sum_xE_{\mathbb P}T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P)\right|^2
 \leq C_\epsilon\left\{
 \frac d{mL_d}+\frac{d^2}{m^2L_d^2}\right\}.                     \tag{15}
\]
Independence and the cell variance bound give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P}\left(\sum_xT_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\right)
 \leq C_\epsilon d^{1/16}
 \left\{\frac{L_d}{m}+\frac{dL_d^2}{m^2}\right\}.               \tag{16}
\]
Because \(m\geq d/(8L_d)\), the second term of (15), divided by \(d/(mL_d)\), is at most eight.  The two terms of (16), divided by \(d/(mL_d)\), are bounded respectively by
\[
 d^{-15/16}L_d^2,
 \qquad 8d^{-15/16}L_d^4,
\]
which are uniformly bounded for integer \(d\geq2\).  Thus
\[
 E_{\mathbb P}\left[
 \left\{\sum_xT_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P)\right\}^2\right]
 \leq C_\epsilon\frac d{mL_d}.                                    \tag{17}
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]\) cannot increase squared distance from \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\in[0,1]\).

Adjoin an infinite independent continuation of the fixed sample.  The ideal uncapped Poisson statistic and the capped randomized statistic in \(\mathrm{def:jackson\mbox{-}factorial\mbox{-}estimator}\) agree on \(\{M\leq n\}\).  Both projected losses are at most one, whereas exponential Markov gives
\[
 \Pr\{M>n\}=\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)>n\}\leq e^{-cn}.       \tag{18}
\]
Equations (17)--(18) bound the randomized fixed-sample risk by
\[
 C_\epsilon\frac d{nL_d}+e^{-cn}.
\]
For \(d\geq2\), the exponential term is at most a universal multiple of \(d/(nL_d)\).  Conditional Jensen for squared loss then shows that the Rao--Blackwellized estimator
\[
 \widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=E(\widetilde V\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)
\]
has no larger risk.

If \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), the estimator is \(1/2\), its risk is at most \(1/4\), and \(d/(nL_d)>1\), so the minimum in the theorem equals one.

It remains to treat \(2\leq d<D_0\).  Conditional on \(\overline N_x=k>0\), the arm count \(\overline N_{ax}\) is binomial with success probability \(\rho_{ax}\geq\epsilon\).  For \(H\sim\operatorname{Bin}(k,\rho)\),
\[
 E\frac{\mathbf1\{H>0\}}H\leq\frac2{k\rho},
 \qquad
 \Pr(H=0)=(1-\rho)^k\leq\frac1{k\rho}.                            \tag{19}
\]
The first inequality follows from \(H^{-1}\mathbf1\{H>0\}\leq2/(H+1)\) and
\[
 E(H+1)^{-1}=\frac{1-(1-\rho)^{k+1}}{(k+1)\rho};
\]
the second follows from \((1-\rho)^k\leq(1+k\rho)^{-1}\).  Conditional binomial variance and the \(0/0=0\) convention imply
\[
 E\{(\widehat\mu_{ax}-\mu_{ax})^2\mid\overline N_x=k\}
 \leq\frac3{k\epsilon}.                                            \tag{20}
\]
The maximum is one-Lipschitz in the sup norm.  Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz followed by (20) yields
\[
 E\left[
 \left\{\sum_x\widehat p_x
 (\max_a\widehat\mu_{ax}-\max_a\mu_{ax})\right\}^2\right]
 \leq\frac{6d}{n\epsilon}.                                         \tag{21}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 E\lVert\widehat p-p\rVert_1^2
 \leq d\sum_x\operatorname{Var}(\widehat p_x)\leq\frac dn.       \tag{22}
\]
Decomposing the empirical-ratio error into the regression term in (21) and the mass-estimation term in (22), and also using that both the estimator and target lie in \([0,1]\), gives risk at most \(C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/n\}\).  Since \(L_d\) is bounded above and below for \(2\leq d<D_0\), this is at most
\[
 C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/(nL_d)\}.
\]
All bounds are uniform over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), so they permit unequal unknown propensities, arbitrary masses, null cells, overlap boundaries, outcome boundaries, and exact ties.  This proves the theorem in every regime.

statements.statement: Every \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\) mapped by \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) has an observed margin in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) with \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), and \(\Psi=1/2+\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1/4\).  From \(n\) draws from each of \(\mathbf P\) and \(\mathbf Q\), an explicit Markov kernel produces exactly \(n\) independent observations from that margin, so \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is at least one sixteenth of the corresponding normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared error.
statements.justification: The exact slice transfers the normalized-distance obstruction upward to the full observed class.
statements.gap: JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 studies the source distance experiment, not this observed cell embedding or its optimal-regression functional.
statements.consumer: The all-estimator converse uses this subclass in the logarithmic normalized-distance regime.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\) and apply \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\).  Summing its four masses gives
\[
 p_x=\sum_{a,y}q_{ay,x}=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{2},\qquad
 s_1(q_x)=s_0(q_x)=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{4}.                               \tag{14}
\]
Thus every occupied cell has \(\pi_x=1/2\), which lies in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\) because \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  On a cell with \(P_x+Q_x>0\),
\[
 \mu_{1x}=\frac{P_x}{P_x+Q_x},\qquad
 \mu_{0x}=\frac{Q_x}{P_x+Q_x}.                                     \tag{15}
\]
Equations (14)--(15) and \(0\leq\mu_{ax}\leq1\) verify every condition of \(\mathrm{def:observed-model-class}\); null cells contribute zero.  By \(\mathrm{def:observed-optimal-value}\),
\[
 \Psi=\frac12\sum_x\max\{P_x,Q_x\}
 =\frac12+\frac14\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1,              \tag{16}
\]
using \(\max(r,s)=(r+s+|r-s|)/2\) and the two simplex constraints.

Let \(X_i^P\sim\mathbf P\) and \(X_i^Q\sim\mathbf Q\), independently for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).  For each \(i\), toss an independent fair source coin.  If it selects \(\mathbf P\), use \(X_i^P\) and choose \((A,Y)=(1,1)\) or \((0,0)\) with equal probabilities; if it selects \(\mathbf Q\), use \(X_i^Q\) and choose \((A,Y)=(1,0)\) or \((0,1)\) with equal probabilities.  The resulting observations are independent and have exactly the masses in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\).

For any observed-law estimator \(\widehat V\), define the randomized distance estimator \(\widehat L=4(\widehat V-1/2)\), and condition it on the two original samples.  Equation (16) and conditional Jensen give
\[
 E_{\mathbf P,\mathbf Q}\left[
 \left\{E(\widehat L\mid X^P,X^Q)-\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1\right\}^2\right]
 \leq16E_{\mathbb P}\left[(\widehat V-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2\right]. \tag{17}
\]
Taking the supremum over \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) and then the infimum over all \(\widehat V\) proves the factor-one-sixteenth reduction.  The kernel uses exactly \(n\) observations and introduces no limiting or support approximation.

statements.statement:
Choose the universal cutoff \(D_0\) sufficiently large.  For every \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n>d^2\), the construction in \(\mathrm{def:dense-moment-matching-construction}\) has even degree \(8L_d\leq K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}<8L_d+2\), amplitude \(a_{n,d}^2=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}d/(128n)\leq1/4\), and, for every \(\theta\in[-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\), an observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+\theta_x)/2\), \(\mu_{0x}=(1-\theta_x)/2\), and \(\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}=1/2+(2d)^{-1}\sum_{x=1}^d\lvert\theta_x\rvert\).  The symmetric measures \(\nu_{0,K}\) and \(\nu_{1,K}\) exist for every even \(K\), match moments through degree \(K\), and have absolute-moment gap \(2E_K\) with \(E_K\asymp K^{-1}\).  Consequently \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}=a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\asymp a_{n,d}/K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\).  Writing \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), the one-cell likelihood identity under \(\theta_x=0\) is \(E_0[L_{\theta_x}L_{\theta_x'}]=\exp(\lambda_{n,d}\theta_x\theta_x')\); hence moment matching and tensorization give
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d})
\leq d\left\{\sum_{r=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda_{n,d}a_{n,d}^2)^r}{r!}\right\}^{1/2}
\leq d\left\{\frac{(e/64)^{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}}{1-e/64}\right\}^{1/2}\leq\frac1{16}.
\]
Under either product prior, \(\operatorname{Var}[\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}]\leq a_{n,d}^2/(4d)\), and \(D_0\) can be chosen so that each prior assigns probability at most \(1/8\) to a deviation of the target from its prior mean exceeding \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}/4\).  The two fuzzy hypotheses therefore imply \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_\epsilon(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2\geq c_\epsilon d/[nK_d^{\mathrm{lb}}]\).  Finally, applying any fixed-sample estimator to the first \(n\) observations whenever an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) total count is at least \(n\) yields \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}-P\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}\geq c_\epsilon d/[n\log(ed)]\), after decreasing \(c_\epsilon\).
statements.justification: This lemma derives membership, exact mixture distance, target concentration, fuzzy testing, and de-Poissonization for the dense observed subclass.
statements.gap: CaiLow2011L1 supplies only the approximation-dual priors; the observed sign experiment and its target scaling are derived here.
statements.consumer: The all-estimator theorem uses this lemma in the superquadratic-sample regime.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(K=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_d\rceil\).  Then \(K\) is even and
\[
 8L_d\leq K<8L_d+2.                                                  \tag{18}
\]
With \(\lambda=\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), the construction gives
\[
 a_{n,d}^2=\frac K{64\lambda}=\frac{Kd}{128n}<\frac K{128d}.
\]
Because \(K=O(\log d)\), a universal \(D_0\) makes this at most \(1/4\) for every \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n>d^2\).

For \(|\theta_x|\leq a_{n,d}\leq1/2\), the two Bernoulli means in \(\mathrm{def:dense-moment-matching-construction}\) lie in \([1/4,3/4]\); its observed margin has \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), and binary conditional means in \([0,1]\).  Thus \(\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), since \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  The definition of \(\Psi\) gives
\[
 \Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
 =\frac1d\sum_x\max\left\{\frac{1+\theta_x}{2},\frac{1-\theta_x}{2}\right\}
 =\frac12+\frac1{2d}\sum_x|\theta_x|.                              \tag{19}
\]

The cited leaf \(\mathrm{lem:cai-low-absolute-moment-priors}\) supplies, for this even \(K\), the symmetric measures with matching moments through \(K\), absolute-moment gap \(2E_K\), and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) for which \(c/K\leq E_K\leq C/K\).  Scaling by \(a=a_{n,d}\) and using (19) yields
\[
 \Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}=\frac1{2d}\,d\,(2aE_K)=aE_K
 \asymp\frac aK.                                                     \tag{20}
\]

In the \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) experiment, Poisson splitting makes the two sign counts in one cell independent with means \(\lambda(1+\theta_x)/2\) and \(\lambda(1-\theta_x)/2\).  Relative to \(\theta_x=0\), their likelihood ratio is
\[
 L_{\theta_x}=(1+\theta_x)^{N_+}(1-\theta_x)^{N_-}.
\]
The Poisson generating function gives the exact identity
\[
 E_0(L_{\theta_x}L_{\theta_x'})
 =\exp(\lambda\theta_x\theta_x').                                  \tag{21}
\]
Let \(h_0,h_1\) be the one-cell mixtures under the two scaled priors and \(h_\circ\) the density at \(\theta_x=0\).  Expanding (21) into its nonnegative power series and using cancellation of moments through \(K\) gives
\[
 \int\frac{(h_1-h_0)^2}{h_\circ}
 =\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}\frac{\lambda^r}{r!}
   \{E_1\theta_x^r-E_0\theta_x^r\}^2
 \leq4\sum_{r=K+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda a^2)^r}{r!}.           \tag{22}
\]
Here each remaining moment difference has absolute value at most \(2a^r\).  Cauchy--Schwarz bounds one-cell total variation by the square root of the tail in (22), because its usual factor \(1/2\) cancels the factor \(2\).  Independence across cells under the product priors and telescoping of product measures therefore yield
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d})
 \leq d\left\{\sum_{r=K+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda a^2)^r}{r!}\right\}^{1/2}. \tag{23}
\]
Since \(\lambda a^2=K/64\) and \(r!\geq(r/e)^r\), for \(r\geq K+1\),
\[
 \frac{(\lambda a^2)^r}{r!}\leq(e/64)^r.
\]
Using \(K\geq8\log(ed)\), (23) is at most
\[
 d\left\{\frac{(e/64)^{K+1}}{1-e/64}\right\}^{1/2}\leq\frac1{16} \tag{24}
\]
after increasing \(D_0\).

Under either product prior, coordinate independence and (19) imply
\[
 \operatorname{Var}[\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}]
 =\frac1{4d^2}\sum_x\operatorname{Var}(|\theta_x|)
 \leq\frac{a^2}{4d}.                                                 \tag{25}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality, obtained by applying Markov's inequality to the squared centered target, and (20) bound either prior probability outside radius \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}/4\) by
\[
 \frac{16(a^2/4d)}{a^2E_K^2}=\frac4{dE_K^2}leq C\frac{K^2}{d}\leq\frac18 \tag{26}
\]
for the same sufficiently large \(D_0\).

Let \(r_\star\) be the larger integrated squared risk of an arbitrary estimator under the two priors, and test the prior index by thresholding the estimator at the midpoint of the two target means.  On the concentration event in (26), estimation error smaller than \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}/4\) forces a correct test.  Markov's inequality therefore bounds the sum of the two testing errors by
\[
 \frac14+\frac{32r_\star}{(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2}.
\]
For every test this sum is at least \(1-\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_0,\mathbb M_1)\geq15/16\), by integration against a common dominating measure.  Hence
\[
 r_\star\geq c(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2
 \geq c\frac{a^2}{K^2}=c\frac1{\lambda K}=c\frac d{nK}.           \tag{27}
\]
All prior observation laws lie in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), so (27) lower-bounds \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\).

Finally clip any fixed-\(n\) estimator to \([0,1]\), which cannot increase its loss.  Apply it to the first \(n\) observations of a \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) sample when at least \(n\) observations are present, and output zero otherwise.  Its Poisson risk is at most its fixed-sample risk plus \(P\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}\).  The Poisson lower-tail Chernoff bound is \(e^{-n/4}\).  Taking infima and using (18) gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq c\frac d{nL_d}-e^{-n/4}
 \geq c'\frac d{nL_d},                                               \tag{28}
\]
where the last inequality is uniform for \(d\geq D_0,n>d^2\) after one further increase of \(D_0\).  This proves every assertion.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that the observed-law minimax risk satisfies \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\).  This covers all measurable estimators over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) by splicing the dense Poisson moment-matching subclass when \(n>d^2\), the exact normalized \(L_1\) subclass when \(d/\log(ed)\leq n\leq d^2\), and null-cell padding plus a regular two-point subclass in the saturated and bounded-alphabet regimes.
statements.justification: The lower splice certifies the logarithmic gain as sharp for every measurable estimator on the full observed class.
statements.gap: JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 covers the normalized-distance slice only under logarithmic size conditions; the dense sign and padded regimes close the remaining ranges.
statements.consumer: No alternative observed-data estimator can uniformly beat the Jackson--factorial exponent.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(L_d=\log(ed)\).  We first give a regular observed-law submodel used below.  Put all mass on \(X=1\), take \(A\) fair, fix \(\mu_{01}=0\), and compare \(\mu_{11}=1/2\) with \(\mu_{11}=1/2+\delta\), where \(\delta=1/(8\sqrt n)\).  Both binary laws belong to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), including after padding with null cells.  Their \(\Psi\)-values differ by \(\delta\).  Their one-observation chi-square divergence, computed from the two affected probabilities \(1/4\pm\delta/2\), is
\[
 \chi^2(\mathbb P_1,\mathbb P_0)
 =\frac{(\delta/2)^2}{1/4}+\frac{(\delta/2)^2}{1/4}=2\delta^2.
\]
Product expansion and \(1+t\leq e^t\) give
\[
 \chi^2(\mathbb P_1^n,\mathbb P_0^n)
 =(1+2\delta^2)^n-1\leq e^{1/32}-1.                                \tag{29}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz against \(\mathbb P_0^n\) implies \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_1^n,\mathbb P_0^n)\leq\tfrac12\sqrt{e^{1/32}-1}<1/4\).  Thresholding an arbitrary estimator at the target midpoint, and applying Markov's inequality to squared error under the two laws, therefore yields
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq c/n.                               \tag{30}
\]
Indeed the sum of testing errors is at least \(1-\operatorname{TV}>3/4\), whereas it is at most eight times the larger squared risk divided by \(\delta^2\).

We now cover four exhaustive regimes.  If \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n>d^2\), \(\mathrm{lem:dense-moment-matching-lower}\) gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq c\frac d{nL_d};                    \tag{31}
\]
the ratio is below one in this regime.

Suppose \(d\geq D_0\) and \(d/L_d\leq n\leq d^2\).  The cited \(\mathrm{lem:jhw-poisson-l1-lower}\), applied with alphabet \(d\) and Poisson means \(2n\), has its hypotheses satisfied with universal constants: \(n\geq d/L_d\) and \(\log(en)\leq\log(ed^2)\leq2L_d\).  It gives the Poissonized two-sample lower bound \(c d/[n\log(en)]\geq c'd/(nL_d)\).  Given a fixed-\(n\) two-sample estimator clipped to \([0,2]\), apply it to the first \(n\) observations from each of two independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) samples when both totals exceed \(n\), and output zero otherwise.  The two Poisson lower-tail probabilities are at most \(2e^{-n/4}\); bounded loss therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\geq c\frac d{nL_d}-Ce^{-n/4}
 \geq c'\frac d{nL_d},                                              \tag{32}
\]
after increasing \(D_0\), uniformly because \(n\geq d/L_d\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:equal-propensity-l1-reduction}\) transfers (32), with factor \(1/16\), to \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,epsilon}\).  The embedded margins are a subclass of \(\mathcal D_{d,epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), so this restriction lower-bounds the supremum over the full observed class.

If \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), the desired scale equals one.  For every sufficiently large \(n\), put \(s_n=\lfloor n\log(en)\rfloor\).  The regime implies \(d>nL_d>n\log(en)\), since it first implies \(d>n\) and hence \(L_d>\log(en)\).  Thus \(2\leq s_n\leq d\).  Also \(s_n\asymp n\log(en)\), so
\[
 n\geq c\frac{s_n}{\log(es_n)},\qquad \log(en)\leq C\log(es_n)   \tag{33}
\]
with universal constants.  The cited \(L_1\) lower lemma at alphabet \(s_n\), followed by the same fixed/Poisson transfer and the exact reduction, gives a positive constant.  Padding the remaining \(d-s_n\) cells by zeros preserves both the observation law and \(\Psi\), hence
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,epsilon}\geq c.                                 \tag{34}
\]
For the finitely many smaller \(n\), use the preceding two-point pair with the fixed separation \(1/(8\sqrt{n_0})\), where \(n_0\) is the finite cutoff.  Equation (29) then remains uniformly bounded for \(n\leq n_0\), while the target gap is a fixed positive constant; decreasing \(c\) proves (34) there as well.

Finally, if \(2\leq d<D_0\), (30) applies.  Since \(d/L_d\) is bounded above and away from zero on this finite set, there is a universal constant depending only on the fixed cutoff such that
\[
 \frac cn\geq c'\min\left\{1,\frac d{nL_d}\right\}.              \tag{35}
\]
Equations (31)--(35) cover every \(n\geq1,d\geq2\).  Every hard margin has propensity \(1/2\), so it lies in the full observed class for each fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Decreasing a single constant over the finitely many cutoffs proves the theorem for all measurable estimators.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_\epsilon\leq C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\),
\[
c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\leq\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]
\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}.
\]
Through \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\), the same risk frontier applies to the causal optimal-treatment value over all causal completions whose observed margins range over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact observed-law minimax scale and then transfers it to the causal estimand by a proved equivalence.

statements.proof_tex:
The last inequality in the display is \(\mathrm{thm:jackson\mbox{-}factorial\mbox{-}upper}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}risk}\), \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the infimum of worst-case risks over all measurable estimators.  Since \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) is one such measurable estimator,
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \leq\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
 E_{\mathbb P}\left[
 (\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2\right].
\]
The first inequality is \(\mathrm{thm:all\mbox{-}estimator\mbox{-}lower}\).  Concatenating these three inequalities proves the displayed frontier for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\).

For the causal conclusion, \(\mathrm{prop:identification\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}extension}\) proves that the observed margins of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) fill all of \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\mathrm{prop:causal\mbox{-}optimal\mbox{-}value\mbox{-}corollary}\) proves
\[
 V^\star(P)=\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}.
\]
Thus the observation experiments and targets coincide under the surjective completion map.  The causal statement is consequently a corollary of the statistical frontier, rather than an equality imposed by definition.

statements.statement: The matched frontier recovers the banked parent as a corollary on the identical class: uniformly over \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\), the new upper rate is at most a constant multiple of \(d/n\), while its lower rate is at least a constant multiple of \(\min\{1,\sqrt d/n+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). For every \(2\leq d<D_0\), \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\). Separately, for every bounded sequence of alphabets, \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}=\Theta_\epsilon(n^{-1})\).
statements.justification: This explicit corner check establishes that the run is an estimation refinement of the parent rather than a different model or estimand.
statements.gap: The parent leaves a nonmatching bracket and an unresolved consistency region; this proposition records exactly how every certified parent conclusion is retained.
statements.consumer: Downstream users of the parent bracket can substitute the matched rate without changing their causal assumptions or scalar target.
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 r_{n,d}=\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\},
 \qquad a=d/[n\log(ed)].
\]
Since \(\log(ed)\geq1\), a two-case check according as \(d\geq n\) or \(d<n\) gives \(r_{n,d}\leq d/n\).

Next,
\[
 \frac{\sqrt d/n}{d/[n\log(ed)]}=\frac{\log(ed)}{\sqrt d}
\]
is bounded uniformly over integers \(d\geq2\).  If \(a>1\), the parent minimum is at most one and hence at most \(r_{n,d}=1\).  Suppose \(a\leq1\).  If \(n\geq d\), then \(\log(en)\geq\log(ed)\), so
\[
 \frac d{n\log(en)}\leq a.
\]
If \(n<d\), put \(t=d/n>1\).  The inequality \(a\leq1\) says
\[
 t\leq\log(ed)=\log(en)+\log t.
\]
For \(t\geq2\), \(\log t\leq t/2\), hence \(t\leq2\log(en)\); the case \(1<t<2\) obeys the same conclusion after changing the universal constant.  Therefore \(\log(ed)\leq C\log(en)\), and \(d/[n\log(en)]\leq Ca\).  We have proved
\[
 \min\left\{1,\frac{\sqrt d}{n}+\frac d{n\log(en)}\right\}
 \leq C r_{n,d}.                                                     \tag{23}
\]
Applying \(\mathrm{thm:matched\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}frontier}\) to these deterministic comparisons proves that the new upper rate is bounded by a constant multiple of \(d/n\) and that the new lower rate dominates the stated parent lower expression on the identical model class.

The equality \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\) for \(2\leq d<D_0\) is the first branch of \(\mathrm{def:jackson\mbox{-}factorial\mbox{-}estimator}\).  Finally, along a sequence for which \(2\leq d\leq D<\infty\), the quantity \(d/\log(ed)\) is bounded above and bounded away from zero.  The matched frontier therefore gives
\[
 c_{\epsilon,D}n^{-1}\leq\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \leq C_{\epsilon,D}n^{-1}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), which is the asserted bounded-alphabet parametric conclusion.

statements.statement: Along arbitrary sequences \(n\to\infty\) with \(d=d_n\geq2\), uniform consistency for estimating \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) over \(\mathcal D_{d,epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is possible if and only if \(d=o(n\log(en))\).  Moreover, \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,epsilon}=\Theta_\epsilon(n^{-1})\) if and only if \(d=O(1)\).  By \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\) and observed-margin surjectivity, the same two equivalences hold for estimating \(V^\star(P)\) over \(\mathcal P_{d,epsilon}\).
statements.justification: These equivalences give the exact consistency and parametric phase boundaries for the observed experiment and its causal completions.

statements.consumer: A categorical-adjustment workflow can decide whether its growing table permits uniformly reliable scalar reporting.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{thm:matched\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}frontier}\), uniform consistency is equivalent to
\[
 \frac d{n\log(ed)}\longrightarrow0.                               \tag{24}
\]
We prove that (24) is equivalent to \(d=o(n\log(en))\).  Put \(t=d/n\) and \(L_n=\log(en)\).  If \(t/L_n\to0\), then on any subsequence with \(d\geq n\),
\[
 \log(ed)\geq L_n,
 \qquad
 \frac d{n\log(ed)}\leq\frac t{L_n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
On a subsequence with \(d<n\), if \(d\geq\sqrt n\), then \(\log(ed)\geq L_n/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), so
\[
 \frac d{n\log(ed)}\leq\frac2{L_n}\longrightarrow0;
\]
if \(d<\sqrt n\), that ratio is at most \(n^{-1/2}\).  Thus (24) follows.

Conversely, assume (24).  If \(t<1\), then \(t/L_n\leq1/L_n\to0\).  If \(t\geq1\), define
\[
 \eta_n=\frac{t}{L_n+\log t}.
\]
Because \(L_n+\log t=\log(ed)\), equation (24) says \(\eta_n\to0\).  Since \(\log t\leq t\), eventually \(\eta_n\log t\leq t/2\).  The identity
\[
 t=\eta_nL_n+\eta_n\log t
\]
then gives \(t/L_n\leq2\eta_n\to0\).  This proves the consistency equivalence.

Multiplying the matched frontier by \(n\) shows that parametric mean-squared risk is equivalent, up to constants, to boundedness above and away from zero of
\[
 n\min\left\{1,\frac d{n\log(ed)}\right\}.                         \tag{25}
\]
If \(d=O(1)\) and \(d\geq2\), then \(d/\log(ed)\) is bounded above and away from zero, so (25) is bounded above and away from zero for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Conversely, if \(d\to\infty\) along a subsequence, then either the minimum in (25) equals one, in which case (25) equals \(n\to\infty\), or it equals \(d/[n\log(ed)]\), in which case (25) equals
\[
 \frac d{\log(ed)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus parametric mean-squared risk holds exactly for bounded alphabets.

Finally, \(\mathrm{prop:identification\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}extension}\) gives surjectivity of \(P\mapsto\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) from \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) onto \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\mathrm{prop:causal\mbox{-}optimal\mbox{-}value\mbox{-}corollary}\) gives equality of the causal and observed targets.  Hence the causal and observed minimax experiments have identical attainable worst-case risks, and both equivalences transfer to estimation of \(V^\star(P)\) over \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\).

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), consistency and armwise conditional exchangeability imply
\[
 V^\star(P)=\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}
 =\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}.
\]
Thus the observed-law target is the unrestricted optimal-treatment value for every causal completion in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), while the minimax theorems themselves require only the observed law to lie in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
statements.justification: This corollary keeps the causal estimand distinct from the observed-law functional and proves their equality under the stated causal assumptions.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete explicitly separates its observed regression functional from its causal interpretation; this proposition supplies the corresponding completion and equality for the optimal-regression maximum.
statements.consumer: Causal applications may invoke the minimax frontier only after checking consistency and armwise exchangeability.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) and put \(\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}(P)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:model-class}\), \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  For an occupied cell \(x\), its overlap probabilities are positive, and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional-exchangeability}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) give, separately for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 E_P\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}
 =E_P\{Y(a)\mid A=a,X=x\}
 =E_P(Y\mid A=a,X=x)=\mu_{ax}.                                     \tag{6}
\]
The first equality in (6) is armwise conditional independence; the second is consistency on \(\{A=a\}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:oracle-value}\), finite-support conditioning and (6) imply
\[
 V^\star(P)=\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_x\max_a\mu_{ax}.
\]
Null-cell summands vanish, so \(\mathrm{def:observed-optimal-value}\) identifies the last display with \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\).  This proves the causal equality rather than placing it in either definition.

sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin of \(P\).
sampling_model.units: \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with unrestricted categorical cell masses \(p_x\), including null cells.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Auxiliary Poisson thinning creates independent pilot and evaluation counts; pilot-local tensor Jackson approximation of the globally Lipschitz cell extension is lifted by centered factorial moments, clipped locally, projected globally, and Rao--Blackwellized conditional on all \(n\) observations.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=E[\Pi_{[0,1]}\{\sum_{x=1}^dT_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\}\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n]\), with \(\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\asymp_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\); under the causal corollary, \(\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}=V^\star(P)\).
target_estimand: \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^dp_x\max_a\mu_{ax}\); when \(\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) for a consistent, armwise-exchangeable causal completion, \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=V^\star(P)=E_P[\max_aE_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}]\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper defines the unrestricted observed binary-outcome model by at most \(d\) categorical cells, cell propensities in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and regressions in \([0,1]\), and proves estimation bounds for the linear ATE functional while separating its causal interpretation.
The paper constructs minimax-rate estimators for normalized two-distribution \(L_1\) distance by local polynomial approximation and proves the associated large-alphabet lower rate.
The paper pairs moment-matched priors with best approximation of absolute value and constructs asymptotically sharp estimators for a Gaussian nonsmooth functional.
The paper characterizes pathwise differentiability of the optimal value and gives online one-step inference at certain exceptional laws.
The paper obtains asymptotic inference for optimal policy values through softmax smoothing under controlled near-tie density and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper constructs a local-moment estimator of a distribution up to permutation and proves plug-in universality for several symmetric discrete-distribution functionals.

tldr: Relative to the banked parent \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_optimal\_value\_minimax\_diagonal\_adaptive\_ratio}/\texttt{tv}\), this estimation upgrade replaces the certified \(d/n\) empirical-ratio upper bound by an explicit all-data Jackson--factorial estimator and targets a matched finite-sample risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\asymp_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\). A globally Lipschitz extension of the cell oracle permits one pilot-local tensor Jackson polynomial to handle null cells, off-cone pilots, unequal propensities, boundary means, and exact ties; centered factorial moments, local clipping, Poisson coupling, and Rao--Blackwellization yield the upper bound, while a dense moment-matching experiment, the exact normalized \(L_1\) slice, and padding yield the all-regime converse. The result settles uniform consistency exactly at \(d=o(n\log(en))\) and retains parametric mean-squared error exactly for bounded \(d\).

project_justification.gap: The banked parent proves a global lower envelope but certifies only \(d/n\) achievability, leaving a factor as large as a logarithm and the entire region between \(d=o(n)\) and \(d=o(n\log n)\) unresolved. Published discrete causal work treats linear targets, while published nonsmooth large-alphabet work treats normalized probability coordinates rather than observational ratios.
project_justification.niche: The oracle maximum is a degree-one homogeneous functional of four observed cell masses. Its extension to the whole orthant is globally Lipschitz, so a positive tensor Jackson convolution can adapt pointwise at the cone vertex while retaining an exponential coefficient envelope in a centered local basis.
project_justification.fill: Relative to \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_optimal\_value\_minimax\_diagonal\_adaptive\_ratio}/\texttt{tv}\), the estimation-axis delta is the named all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) with uniform risk \(d/[n\log(ed)]\), plus a matching all-measurable-estimator lower bound and the resulting exact consistency boundary. The same assumptions and target are retained, and for every \(2\leq d<D_0\) the estimator reduces exactly to the parent's empirical-ratio estimator.

related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete} [reused from parent], Introduction, Theorems 1--2, and Discussion, formulate the same structure-free categorical adjustment problem and prove a logarithmically separated minimax analysis for linear treatment-specific means; their target has no maximum or tie surface. Jiao, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoHanWeissman2018L1} [reused from parent], Introduction, Theorem 3, Construction 2, Theorem 6, and Section VI, show that approximation must follow the equality diagonal for \(L_1\) distance and supply the normalized-distance lower theorem used on the exact equal-propensity slice; their unknown--unknown upper estimator does not apply to four observational masses with unknown arm denominators. Cai and Low, \cite{CaiLow2011L1} [reused from parent], Lemma 1 and Sections 3.1--4, provide the approximation--moment dual for the absolute-value cusp and the fuzzy-hypothesis template adapted in the dense lower experiment. Luedtke and van der Laan, \cite{LuedtkeVanderLaan2016OptimalValue} [reused from parent], Theorem 1 and Sections 4--7, characterize local nonregularity and online inference for the same scalar value, but do not analyze a growing unrestricted alphabet. Whitehouse, Chen, Austern, and Syrgkanis, \cite{WhitehouseChenAusternSyrgkanis2025} [reused from parent], the static-treatment theorem and controlled-density lemma, regularize the maximum by softmax; their condition permits an atom at an exact tie but restricts near ties and nuisance rates, so it does not provide a uniform result for the present class. Han, Jiao, and Weissman, \cite{HanJiaoWeissman2018Local} [new], Introduction and Sections 2--3, establish cell localization and moment reconstruction for symmetric functionals, but their quotient forgets the four-coordinate grouping needed by causal ratios. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015Functionals}, provide the earlier polynomial/factorial split-sample architecture. Wei, \cite{Wei2026OffPolicy}, gives the most recent adjacent optimal-value inference result in a trajectory experiment; its efficiency and stability theory does not subsume the present independent categorical minimax problem.
technical_internal_limitation: The estimator is explicit as a measurable Rao--Blackwellized finite-sample rule, but the conditional integration over auxiliary markings and the tensor coefficient calculation are not claimed to run in near-linear time or to be numerically stable at machine precision. The main mathematical kill test is joint: the same Jackson polynomial must satisfy both the vertex-adaptive approximation inequality and the centered coefficient envelope, and pilot-failure moments must retain the local scale \(\sqrt{p_xL_d/n}+L_d/n\).
honest_scope: The formal target is the scalar value of the unrestricted oracle policy, not regret of a learned policy and not uniform confidence intervals. Fixed overlap is maintained; vanishing overlap, growing treatment count, and sharp leading constants remain outside the theorem. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:equal-propensity-l1-reduction}\) is only a lower-bound sanity slice. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:parent-reduction}\) records the strict refinement: the model and estimand are identical to the parent, \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\) only for \(2\leq d<D_0\), the matched rate implies the parent's bracket, and bounded alphabets retain minimax risk \(\Theta_\epsilon(n^{-1})\). The exact constant is exposed separately in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp-overlap-constant}\).
